deep.reconstruction:
This folio is a working draft of passages from Riemann's 1851 Göttingen dissertation, 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. It contains four separate drafts.

(A) Branch points (draft of dissertation Art. 14).
- Near a branch point O' of order n-1 over z = z', Riemann introduces the local variable zeta = (z - z')^(1/n).
- The n sheets meeting at O' are pieces whose images in the zeta-plane fit together into a neighbourhood. That image is a schlicht surface, i.e. one spread simply (single-sheeted) over the plane A.
- The correspondence O <-> zeta is one-to-one. So any quantity defined pointwise on T is also a function of zeta.
- If w is a complex-analytic function of z (dw/dz independent of the direction of dz), then dw/dzeta = (dw/dz)(dz/dzeta) = n zeta^(n-1) dw/dz. This is also direction-independent, so w is analytic in zeta. [The explicit chain-rule step is my addition.]
- Hence the results of Arts. 11-12 (removable singularities and poles for single-valued functions) apply in the variable zeta. This gives the theorem stated on the page:
  - If w becomes infinite as O -> O', it does so like an inverse power of the distance, with exponent m/n.
  - Adding a1 (z-z')^(-1/n) + ... + am (z-z')^(-m/n), with suitable complex constants a_k, makes it continuous at O'. The page calls the a_k 'willkürlich' (arbitrary); they are in fact determined by w.
  - Corollary: if (z-z')^(1/n) w -> 0 as O -> O', then w is continuous there. In zeta-language: zeta·w -> 0 implies the singularity is removable (the Riemann removable-singularity criterion).

(B) Dirichlet principle (draft of Art. 17).
- Omega = ∫∫_T [(alpha_x - beta_y)^2 + (alpha_y + beta_x)^2] dT, with beta fixed and alpha varying in an admissible class.
- Omega is finite for some alpha, varies continuously with alpha, and is always >= 0.
- Riemann concludes that Omega must attain a minimum for at least one form of alpha.

(C) First variation via Green's theorem (draft of Art. 18).
- Write u for alpha and u' for the variation.
- Exclude by small boundaries (as in Art. 7) all parts and points where u_x - beta_y and u_y + beta_x are discontinuous. Call the excluded part T'' and the rest T'.
- The cross term ∫_T' [(u_x - beta_y) u'_x + (u_y + beta_x) u'_y] dS is transformed by Green's theorem in the form ∫(dX/dx + dY/dy) dT = -∫(X dx/dp + Y dy/dp) ds, with p the inward normal (the page cites 'Art. 6').
- Take X = (u_x - beta_y) u' and Y = (u_y + beta_x) u'. Then dX/dx + dY/dy = u' Δu + (u_x - beta_y) u'_x + (u_y + beta_x) u'_y, because the mixed beta terms cancel. [This cancellation is my explicit step.]
- On the boundary, using x_p = y_s and y_p = -x_s, the boundary integrand reduces to (du/dp - dbeta/ds) u'.
- Result: ∫_T' (...) dS = -∫ u' (u_xx + u_yy) dS - ∫ (du/dp - dbeta/ds) u' ds, exactly as on the page.

(D) Cross-cuts (draft of the definitions in Art. 6).
- A dissection of a surface by several cross-cuts (Querschnitte) is always to be understood as successive.
- Each new cut is made in the surface already produced by the previous cuts.
- This underlies the definition of the order of connectivity.

The previous page is unrelated: a schedule for the Göttingen physics seminar.
errors: The minimum argument in (B) is unjustified: Omega >= 0 gives only an infimum, not an attained minimum. This is the gap in Riemann's use of the Dirichlet principle criticised by Weierstrass (1870) and repaired by Hilbert (1900).
In (C) the page says to substitute (du/dy + dbeta/dx) for Y without the factor u'. To obtain the stated result Y must be (u_y + beta_x) u', as X includes u'. This is a slip of the pen.
In (A) the coefficients a_1..a_m are called 'willkürliche' (arbitrary) complex quantities. To cancel the singularity they are determined by w; only the form of the expression is general.
The draft cites 'Art. 6' for Green's theorem and 'Art. 7' for excluding singular points; the article numbering is still fluid. A minor inconsistency, not a mathematical error.

results.what: Local uniformizing parameter zeta=(z-z')^(1/n) at a branch point; w analytic in zeta; singularities at branch points are Puiseux-type poles with principal part sum a_k (z-z')^(-k/n); removability if (z-z')^(1/n) w -> 0
results.modern_name: Local coordinate (uniformizer) at a ramification point; Laurent/Puiseux expansion; Riemann removable singularity theorem on a Riemann surface
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1851 (dissertation Art. 14); Puiseux 1850 for the series

results.what: Existence of a minimizer of the Dirichlet-type integral Omega because Omega >= 0
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1851/1857 (name from Dirichlet; Gauss, Thomson earlier); rigorous by Hilbert 1900

results.what: First variation of Omega via Green's theorem giving -∫u' Δu dS - ∫(du/dp - dbeta/ds) u' ds
results.modern_name: Green's first identity / Euler-Lagrange equation with natural boundary term
results.usually_credited_to: Green 1828; in this form Riemann 1851 Art. 18

results.modern_name: Cuts defining connectivity / first Betti number

deep.surprise_reason: All the material is a draft of Riemann's published 1851 dissertation (Arts. 6, 14, 17, 18). It offers only minor insight into drafting variants such as wording, article numbering and the u' slip.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y'); u=Function('u')(x,y); b=Function('b')(x,y); v=Function('v')(x,y); X=(diff(u,x)-diff(b,y))*v; Y=(diff(u,y)+diff(b,x))*v; simplify(diff(X,x)+diff(Y,y) - (v*(diff(u,x,2)+diff(u,y,2)) + (diff(u,x)-diff(b,y))*diff(v,x) + (diff(u,y)+diff(b,x))*diff(v,y)))
checkable.asserts: Divergence identity behind Art. 18: the beta cross terms cancel (result 0).
dz/dzeta = n zeta^(n-1), so dw/dzeta = n zeta^(n-1) dw/dz is direction-independent if dw/dz is (result 0).

checkable.sympy: zeta=symbols('zeta'); a1,a2,c0,c1=symbols('a1 a2 c0 c1'); w=a1/zeta+a2/zeta**2+c0+c1*zeta; simplify(w-(a1/zeta+a2/zeta**2))
checkable.asserts: Subtracting the principal part sum a_k zeta^(-k), with zeta=(z-z')^(1/n), leaves a function regular at zeta=0 (result c0+c1*zeta).
Corollary check: for regular w, zeta*w -> 0 (result 0); a pole a/zeta would give zeta*w -> a != 0.

transcription_corrections: In the variation paragraph, 'u' stands for the function earlier called alpha ('Fct. α'); the integrand uses du/dx - dβ/dy and du/dy + dβ/dx.
The phrase transcribed '[-für X-] (∂u/∂x−∂β/∂y)u' [-und-] für X' should read: 'indem man (∂u/∂x − ∂β/∂y)u' für X, und ∂u/∂y + ∂β/∂x für Y setzt'. The u' is missing from Y in the manuscript itself.
The margin number '(50' at the right is the folio number, not part of the text.
'so können daher zu einer zusammenhängenden Abbildung ... zusammengefügt werden': the reading 'zusammengefügt' is plausible from the image.
